_metadata.description: Restructured based on workshop feedback: improved clarity, added cost breakdown, removed unused fields, added validation hints

info.title: InsectAI hardware form - full version
info.description: This questionnaire collects information about hardware devices used for automated insect monitoring. Only the 'Basic information' section is mandatory — all other sections are optional but help make your entry more useful to the community.

sections.title: Submission type
sections.description: Every device in the database is assigned a unique deviceID (e.g. 'AMI-trap_v1_Smith2023'). DeviceIDs are generated automatically from your submission. You can browse existing entries at https://insectai-cost-action.github.io/hardware-db/

questions.title: Is this a new device submission or an update to an existing entry?
questions.description: Select 'New device' if this hardware has never been submitted before. Select 'Update existing entry' if you are providing a revised version or correcting a previous submission.

sections.title: Update existing entry
sections.description: Provide details to identify the existing entry you wish to update.

questions.title: Existing deviceID
questions.description: Enter the deviceID from your previous submission exactly as it appears (e.g. 'AMI-trap_v1_Smith2023'). Check the database landing page if unsure: https://insectai-cost-action.github.io/hardware-db/

questions.title: Reason for update
questions.description: Briefly describe what has changed (e.g. 'new hardware version', 'correcting sensor specs', 'adding missing links').

sections.title: Basic information
sections.description: Core details about the device and its contact person. All fields in this section are required.

questions.title: Contact person name
questions.description: The person who should be contacted about this database entry. This does not have to be the device designer — it can be a project manager, lab lead, or maintainer.

questions.title: Contact person email
questions.description: A valid email address for the contact person above. This will not be publicly displayed; it is used only for database management queries. Format: name@example.com

questions.title: Device name
questions.description: The common or published name of the device (e.g. 'AMI-trap', 'InsectDetect', 'PitfallCam'). If the device has no established name, use a short descriptive label.

questions.title: Device description
questions.description: A short abstract (max 300 characters) explaining what your device is and does. Write for a non-specialist audience, focusing on purpose and key features rather than technical specifications.

sections.title: People and project details
sections.description: Information about the team behind this device, including who designed it, who maintains it, and how to reach them. Separate multiple names or emails with ';'.

questions.title: Person submitting this form (if different from contact)
questions.description: The person filling in this form, if different from the contact person above.

questions.title: Submitter email (if different from contact)
questions.description: Email address of the person submitting this form. Format: name@example.com

questions.title: Institution name(s)
questions.description: The institution(s) affiliated with this device or project. Separate multiple institutions with ';' (e.g. 'University of Edinburgh; NERC').

questions.title: Device designer(s)
questions.description: The person(s) who originally designed or built this device. Separate multiple names with ';' (e.g. 'Alan Turner; Dave Johnson').

questions.title: Device designer email(s)
questions.description: Email address(es) for the designer(s) above, in the same order, separated by ';'. Format: name@example.com

questions.title: Current maintainer name(s)
questions.description: The person(s) currently responsible for maintaining or updating the device design. Leave blank if same as designer. Separate multiple names with ';'.

questions.title: Current maintainer email(s)
questions.description: Email for the maintainer(s) above. Format: name@example.com

questions.title: Estimated project duration and team size
questions.description: Approximate time and effort invested in developing this device (e.g. '2 years, 3 people part-time' or '6 months, 1 person full-time'). This helps others gauge the complexity of similar projects.

sections.title: Device links and documentation
sections.description: Links to external resources about this device. We cannot host files directly — please provide URLs to resources hosted elsewhere (e.g. GitHub, Zenodo, institutional repositories, YouTube).

questions.title: Documentation URL
questions.description: Link to the main documentation or build instructions (e.g. a GitHub repository, wiki, or published guide). Format: https://...

questions.title: Documentation language
questions.description: The primary language of the documentation (e.g. 'English', 'German', 'Spanish').

questions.title: Publication DOI(s)
questions.description: DOI(s) for publications describing this device. Separate multiple DOIs with ';' (e.g. '10.1234/abc; 10.5678/def'). Format: 10.XXXX/...

questions.title: Additional resources
questions.description: Links to any other relevant resources such as YouTube videos, blog posts, datasets, or design files hosted externally. Separate multiple URLs with ';'. Format: https://...

sections.title: Device details
sections.description: Physical and design characteristics of the device.

questions.title: Device version name
questions.description: A label for this specific version of the device (e.g. 'v2.1', '2024-field-edition'). Useful when multiple versions exist.

questions.title: Device licence (e.g. CC-BY-4.0)
questions.description: The licence under which the device design and associated materials are released. Use a standard SPDX identifier where possible (e.g. 'CC-BY-4.0', 'MIT', 'CERN-OHL-S-2.0'). Leave blank if unknown.

questions.title: Device construction type
questions.description: Select all that apply to describe how the device was built.
options: Modified off-the-shelf: Pre-built device with user-made adjustments
Partly custom: Assembled from standard components with custom-designed parts (e.g. 3D-printed enclosure, custom PCB)
Fully custom: Designed and fabricated entirely by the user

questions.title: Unit build cost — hardware only (€)
questions.description: Approximate cost to build one unit of the device (components, PCBs, enclosure, etc.). Exclude labour, consumables, and operational costs.

questions.title: Deployment/seasonal costs — consumables (€)
questions.description: Estimated cost of consumables per deployment season (e.g. batteries, lures, replacement parts, SIM cards).

questions.title: Ongoing software/compute costs (€/year)
questions.description: Annual cost for cloud services, software licences, data storage, or compute resources required to operate the device.

questions.title: Assembly time (human-hours per unit)
questions.description: Approximate number of person-hours needed to assemble one unit of the device from parts.

questions.title: Packaged dimensions for transport (L × W × H cm)
questions.description: Dimensions when the device is packed for transport (e.g. '30 × 20 × 15').

questions.title: Deployed dimensions (L × W × H cm)
questions.description: Dimensions when the device is set up and operational in the field (e.g. '50 × 40 × 120').

questions.title: Primary material
questions.description: The main material used in the device enclosure or structure.

questions.title: Device mobility
questions.description: How the device is positioned in the field.

questions.title: Skills and tools required for construction
questions.description: Select all skills or tools needed to build this device.

sections.title: Component details
sections.description: Details about sensors, processing, power, and connectivity.

questions.title: Sensor type(s)
questions.description: The primary sensing technology used by the device. Select all that apply.

questions.title: Image resolution range (megapixels)
questions.description: Minimum and maximum resolution the sensor supports (e.g. '5–12 MP'). Leave blank if not applicable.

questions.title: Frame rate range (FPS)
questions.description: Minimum and maximum frames per second the device can capture (e.g. '1–30 FPS'). Leave blank if not applicable.

questions.title: Sensor/lens field of view
questions.description: The field of view of the sensor or lens, in degrees or descriptive terms (e.g. '120°', 'wide-angle', '50mm equivalent'). Leave blank if unknown.

questions.title: Available image capture modes
questions.description: Select all capture modes supported by the device.

questions.title: Power source(s)
questions.description: Select all power sources that can be used to operate the device.

questions.title: Power autonomy under continuous use
questions.description: How long the device can run on a single charge or battery set during continuous operation (e.g. '8 hours', '3 days'). Enter 'N/A' if grid-powered only.

questions.title: Power autonomy under standard use
questions.description: How long the device operates between charges or battery changes under typical deployment conditions (e.g. motion-triggered, scheduled intervals). Enter 'N/A' if grid-powered only.

questions.title: Processing unit
questions.description: The main compute component of the device (e.g. 'Raspberry Pi 4', 'NVIDIA Jetson Nano', 'Arduino Uno', 'ESP32', 'microcontroller'). Include model name and version where known.

questions.title: Model/data processing location
questions.description: Where detection or classification models are run. Select all that apply.
options: Offboard processing (data transferred to separate computer)

questions.title: Connectivity
questions.description: Select all connectivity options available on the device.

questions.title: Supported file types
questions.description: Select all data file formats the device can produce.

questions.title: On-device software version and repository link
questions.description: The version of the software running on the device and a link to its source repository, if available (e.g. 'v1.3.2 — https://github.com/org/repo'). Distinct from the hardware version.

questions.title: Attractants used
questions.description: Any attractants used to lure target organisms toward the device (e.g. 'UV light', 'pheromone lure', 'sugar bait', 'none').

sections.title: Maintenance and repairs
sections.description: Information about repairability, maintenance requirements, and firmware updates.

questions.title: Repairability score
questions.description: Rate from 1 (hardest) to 5 (easiest). 1 = requires soldering or specialist tools; 2 = requires tools but no specialist skills; 3 = screwdriver assembly, standard parts; 4 = snap-fit or modular replacement; 5 = fully tool-free, hot-swap components.

questions.title: Recommended maintenance interval
questions.description: How often routine maintenance should be performed and what it involves (e.g. 'Clean lens every 2 weeks', 'Replace desiccant monthly', 'Check seals before each season').

questions.title: Last firmware/software update date
questions.description: The date of the most recent firmware or software update (e.g. '2025-03-15' or 'March 2025').

questions.title: Firmware update method
questions.description: How firmware is delivered to the device.

sections.title: Intended usage scope and operational constraints
sections.description: Information about the target organisms, environments, and operating conditions for this device.

questions.title: Target taxonomic group(s)
questions.description: Select the insect or arthropod groups this device is designed or validated for.

questions.title: Target habitat type(s)
questions.description: Select the habitat(s) where this device is intended to be deployed.

questions.title: Minimum operational temperature (°C)
questions.description: The lowest ambient temperature at which the device functions reliably (e.g. '-10').

questions.title: Maximum operational temperature (°C)
questions.description: The highest ambient temperature at which the device functions reliably (e.g. '45').

questions.title: IP rating or weatherproofing
questions.description: The IP (Ingress Protection) rating if known (e.g. 'IP65', 'IP54'). If no formal rating exists, describe the protection level (e.g. 'splash-proof enclosure', 'fully sealed', 'not weatherproof').

questions.title: Operational environment
questions.description: The primary environment type where the device operates.

questions.title: Minimum target subject size (mm)
questions.description: The smallest organism size the device is designed to detect or image (e.g. '2').

questions.title: Maximum target subject size (mm)
questions.description: The largest organism size the device is designed to detect or image (e.g. '80').

questions.title: Operational costs per season (€)
questions.description: Estimated total running costs for one typical deployment season (e.g. one summer). Include consumables, data plans, cloud storage, transport to site, etc. Exclude the initial hardware build cost.
